change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` setting row exists
findings.body:
`execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` is indexed with no check for an empty result. `embed_category` defaults to `''` (removed from `config/site_settings.yml` in this PR), so a `site_settings` row exists only if an admin changed it. On every fresh database, and on every site that never set it, the join returns zero rows. `[0]` then yields `nil` (or raises `IndexError`, depending on the pg version) and the whole migration fails. The `cmd_tuples > 0` guard a few lines below shows the empty-result case was considered for `embeddable_hosts` but not here. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` is on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`; that row is normally created by `20131022045114_add_uncategorized_category.rb`, so it is less likely to be missing.

Fix: read the result with `.first` or `cmd_tuples` and fall back to `uncategorized_category_id` when it is empty.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw: they are not normalised, not quoted, and may be blank
findings.body:
Each line of the old setting is interpolated straight into SQL (`'#{h}'`). The `before_validation` normalisation in `EmbeddableHost` does not run for raw SQL, so existing entries such as `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234` are stored with the scheme and path. The old code accepted those forms (the removed `allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `^https?://`). The new `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` to `URI(referer).host`, which has no scheme or path, so these rows never match. After upgrade, embedding silently stops for any site whose setting used that form.

Other problems on the same line:
- A host containing `'` breaks the statement and aborts the migration.
- Blank lines or `\r` from `split("\n")` become empty or dirty host rows that show up in the admin UI.

Fix: strip the scheme and path, strip whitespace, skip blank entries, downcase, and use `quote`/`sanitize_sql` when inserting.

The `DELETE` on line 31 also drops `embed_category` when `embeddable_hosts` is empty, so that category choice is lost without any record.

findings.title: A host saved with a port can never match
findings.body: The format validation allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` keeps it, so `example.com:3000` is saved. `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` to `URI(referer).host`, which never includes the port. A host with a port is therefore accepted by the admin UI but never allows embedding. The failure is silent: the row looks valid. Either reject ports in validation or compare against `host:port` when the referer has a non-default port.

findings.title: nil host raises in `before_validation`; controller does not guard missing params or ids
findings.body:
`self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil, before validation can report it. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly (`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23`), so a request without that param gives a 500 instead of a validation error. Likewise `update` and `destroy` call `.first` and then use the result with no nil check (lines 10-11 and 15-16). Deleting a host that another admin already removed returns a 500. The UI always sends a host, so this is reachable by stale pages or crafted requests. Use `host.to_s`/safe navigation in the callback and respond 404 for a missing id.

There is also no uniqueness validation or index on `host`, so duplicates with different categories can be saved. `record_for_host` then silently picks one.

findings.title: Feed-imported topics lose their configured category
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` now takes its category only from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`, and passes nil when the URL's host is not a registered embeddable host. Before this PR every imported topic, including feed topics, went to `SiteSetting.embed_category`. `Jobs::PollFeed#import_topic` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:39`) calls `import` with the feed item's link, and nothing requires that host to be registered as an embeddable host (that list is matched against referers). Topics from the RSS/ATOM feed would then land in Uncategorized with no error. The migration does not help: it only creates category mappings for hosts in the old list (and drops `embed_category` entirely when the list was empty). Please confirm this is intended, or keep a fallback category for feed imports.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between the two files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`, and the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category`. It works only because all fabricators are loaded together. Anyone looking for the category fabricators will not find them, and git history shows the category file as rewritten. Restore `category_fabricator.rb` unchanged and put only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts, and the example now has no host, no `embed_truncate` and no topic embed. It passes only because `embed_truncate` is false and `has_topic_embed?` is false, so its name is misleading. The behaviour change (with `embed_truncate` and an embed, the result is now true even when no host exists) has no test. Remove the example or rename it to match what it checks. The nested describe is also misspelled ("emeddable").

findings.title: Controller specs only check the superclass
findings.body: Both new admin controller specs assert only that the class subclasses `AdminController`. Nothing covers create, update, destroy, the uncategorized fallback when `category_id` is blank, the invalid-host error response, or non-admin access. The migration is also untested. `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` does not cover `record_for_host`, upper-case hosts, ports, or an unregistered host.

findings.title: `update` and `saveChanges` do nothing useful
findings.body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` just re-serialises the unchanged object. The PUT route (`config/routes.rb:139`) and the `saveChanges` action (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5`) are never wired to any template button. Hosts are saved individually via `embeddable-host`. Remove the dead PUT route, action and controller method, or add the intended settings that need saving. The `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` here and in the hosts controller duplicate the filters `Admin::AdminController` already declares.

findings.title: Plural `_ids` hydration is not defensive and differs from the singular branch
findings.body: For `*_ids` keys, the `_ids` array is always deleted, even if some ids are not found. `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for those, so the array can contain undefined entries, whereas the singular branch keeps `_id` when nothing is hydrated. `hydrated || []` is dead code, since `map` always returns an array. A null or non-array `*_ids` value would throw on `.map`. The regex now applies to every `__rest_serializer` payload (`SimilarTopicSerializer`, queued posts, the new embedding serializer). Filter out unresolved entries and guard with `Array.isArray`.

findings.title: Delete has no error handler; new hosts show no category until reload
findings.body:
`destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save`. A failed DELETE (for example a 500 on an already-removed id) leaves the row in place with no message from this component.

Separately, in `save` (line 38) the component sets `category` from `categoryId`. For a new host where the user never picks a category, `categoryId` is null, so `category` is undefined and the badge is empty. The server (`embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25`) stored Uncategorized, and the real category appears only after a reload.

Category deletion also leaves orphaned `embeddable_hosts` rows: `Category` has no association or cleanup for them, so such hosts show a blank badge and import into Uncategorized.

findings.title: `find('fruit', 2)` test asserts against fruit 1's data
findings.body: The pretender route `/fruits/:id` ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]` (`test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:226-228`). The test asks for fruit 2 but receives fruit 1, and the colors assertions pass only because fruit 1 has `color_ids: [1,2]`. Fruit 2 has `[3]`, so the test's apparent intent is not what runs. Either make the route return the fruit matching `:id` or keep the lookup as `find('fruit', 1)`.

contracts.action: Migration copies the `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` site settings into the new table, then deletes both settings
contracts.equivalent_path: Earlier data migrations that read `site_settings` via `execute` (e.g. db/migrate/20140715190552_remove_uncategorized_parents.rb) and `uncategorized_category_id` set in db/migrate/20131022045114_add_uncategorized_category.rb
contracts.before_after: Before: hosts and category live in two site settings. After: one `embeddable_hosts` row per line of the old setting with a single category_id. The settings rows are deleted at line 31. Hosts are inserted verbatim, with no normalisation.
contracts.visible_effect: Admin page /admin/customize/embedding lists migrated hosts. Raw-inserted hosts with a scheme or path never match referers.
contracts.failure_mode: Unguarded `[0]['id']` on an empty result aborts the migration when `embed_category` was never set. The DELETE is in the same transaction as the inserts, so a failure rolls back both. `create_table force: true` drops any existing table. `change` with `execute` has no `down`, so the migration is irreversible and the old setting values cannot be restored after it runs. The DELETE targets rows by fixed name only, which is a bounded target.

contracts.action: Referer check for embedding switched from the site setting to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` in app/models/site_setting.rb, which compared the referer host to each line of the setting after stripping `http(s)://`
contracts.before_after: Before: the setting was matched after stripping the scheme, and a blank setting raised 'embeddable hosts not set'. After: `lower(host) = URI(referer).host` against table rows. An empty table rejects everything through the same InvalidAccess; a nil referer makes `URI(nil)` raise, which `rescue nil` turns into false.
contracts.visible_effect: Embed iframe/comments are rendered only for registered hosts; otherwise InvalidAccess. Hosts with a port can never match.
contracts.failure_mode: No DB error handling is needed. A saved host with a port, or a legacy row with scheme/path, never matches and embedding silently fails.

contracts.action: TopicEmbed.import chooses the topic category from the matching EmbeddableHost
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `category: SiteSetting.embed_category` for every import (embed iframe via TopicRetriever and PollFeed)
contracts.before_after: Before: one global category. After: per-host category via `record_for_host(url)`, nil when the host is unregistered. PostCreator then falls back to Uncategorized, since `find_category` returns nil for a nil category.
contracts.visible_effect: New embedded topics appear in the host's category. Feed-imported topics from unregistered hosts appear in Uncategorized.
contracts.failure_mode: No error. Silent category fallback for feed imports (poll_feed.rb:39 calls import with the item URL and no host check).

contracts.action: Admin adds, edits, or deletes an allowed host in the embedding page
contracts.equivalent_path: Other RestModel save/destroy flows via store.update/createRecord/destroyRecord (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/rest.js.es6) and the admin-prefixed adapter path in discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6
contracts.before_after: New: createRecord('embeddable-host') then save → POST /admin/embeddable_hosts. Hydrated hosts have type `embeddable_host`, which the changed `basePath` maps to the admin prefix, so update and delete use /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id. Server responds with the host JSON; the component sets `category` from the chosen id.
contracts.visible_effect: Row switches from edit to display mode and shows the host and category badge. A save error shows a popup via `popupAjaxError`. A delete error has no handler.
contracts.failure_mode: Rejected save: popup, row stays in edit mode. Rejected delete: no handler, row stays. Server 500 on nil host/missing id as noted in findings. State is loaded once with the route model; leaving and returning re-fetches through `store.find('embedding')`, so there is no stale flag across remounts (`editToggled` is a per-component instance property).

contracts.equivalent_path: Singular `*_id` hydration in the same function, which keeps the `_id` key when the sub-object is not found
contracts.before_after: Before: only `*_id` keys. After: `*_ids` arrays are mapped through `_lookupSubType` and replaced by a plural array property. Unresolved ids leave undefined entries and the `_ids` key is always removed.
contracts.visible_effect: The hosts table renders from `embedding.embeddable_hosts`. Empty list hides the table, with only the Add button shown.
contracts.failure_mode: A null or non-array `*_ids` throws inside the store call, rejecting the route model. The regex change applies to every rest-serialized payload.

summary:
The migration is a blocker: it crashes on any database without an `embed_category` setting row, which includes fresh installs and sites that never set it. The most serious bugs:
- The migration inserts old hosts raw, so legacy `http://…` entries no longer match referers after upgrade.
- Hosts saved with a port can never match a referer.
- Feed-imported topics now fall back to Uncategorized when their host isn't registered.

Smaller items:
- Nil params and ids give 500s in the admin controller.
- The fabricator files have their contents swapped.
- A topic spec has a stale name and tests nothing.
- The controller specs only check the superclass.
- The PUT route and `saveChanges` are dead code.
- Plural `_ids` hydration is not defensive.
- A pretender test asserts against the wrong fruit.

I only read the repository and did not run any code."
